placements.title: Authority over what the organization remembers and forgets
placements.frame: What governs which knowledge the organization retains and which it discards?
placements.why: Both directives — to forget a prior decision and to remove all knowledge of a database migration — establish an organizational concern with who controls institutional memory, naming a strata category for knowledge governance that nothing existing covers.

placements.title: Authority to erase what was known
placements.frame: When does the unilateral directive to discard shared knowledge reveal the boundaries of institutional memory?
placements.why: Both segments are unhedged imperative directives commanding erasure of specific institutional knowledge — a prior decision and a database migration — enacting the speaker's autonomous authority over what persists. This names a thematic subject about the unilateral disposal of shared knowledge that future envelopes may continue to feed.
